title: A placement policy directs each workload to the platform where it creates the greatest enterprise value
intro: Fabric should complement UHG’s established data ecosystem rather than become the default destination for every workload. Transparent criteria will guide placement, interoperability, and future migration decisions.
decision_and_platform_hypotheses: Evaluate capability fit, data gravity, PHI and security, performance, cost, platform maturity, and skill alignment
Apply mandatory architecture and compliance gates before evaluating relative platform advantages
Document the decision, accountable owner, approved pattern, dependencies, and exceptions
Fabric: Qualified Microsoft-aligned BI, semantic, SQL, sharing, real-time, and
Databricks UDLP: Existing and best-fit data engineering, advanced analytics,
Snowflake SDRP: Existing and best-fit governed analytics, reporting, and data-sharing workloads
Remain authoritative systems of record and integrate through approved patterns
rectangle_5: Consume data where it resides when practical, minimizing unnecessary duplication, latency, control gaps,
Select shortcuts, sharing, virtualization, replication, or movement based on workload requirements
Preserve consistent contracts, cataloging, lineage, security, ownership, and service expectations across platforms
